subject: Meteorology
title: The Urban Heat Island
description: A quick win: understand The Urban Heat Island.

hook.text: Cities can be 5–10°C warmer than surrounding countryside—concrete and asphalt trap and radiate heat.

buildup.text: Dark roofs, roads, and buildings absorb solar energy all day—then release it slowly at night.

discovery.text: Less vegetation means less cooling from evapotranspiration—trees act as natural air conditioners.

twist.text: Urban heat islands create their own weather—cities can trigger more thunderstorms downwind.

climax.text: Cool roofs and urban forests can reduce the effect—painting roofs white in NYC cut indoor temps by 2°C.

punchline.text: Cities build their own heat—and can engineer it away.

quiz.question: What causes the urban heat island effect?
options: Dark surfaces absorb and radiate heat
